questions.title: Progressive overload
questions.prompt: Explain the principle of progressive overload in strength training, how a beginner can apply it safely, and why recovery matters. (General education, not medical advice.)
questions.modelAnswer: Progressive overload means gradually increasing the demand on muscles — more weight, reps, sets or better control — so the body keeps adapting. Beginners can add small increments when they complete all target reps with good form. Adaptation happens during recovery, so sleep, rest days and adequate food matter as much as the workouts; jumping too fast raises injury risk.

questions.title: Why sleep matters for performance
questions.prompt: Explain why sleep matters for learning and physical performance, and suggest three practical habits for better sleep. (General education, not medical advice.)

expectedConcepts.label: Consistent schedule, less screen light, cool dark room

questions.modelAnswer: During sleep the brain consolidates what you learned and the body repairs tissue, so poor sleep hurts both focus and training progress. Habits: a consistent sleep and wake time, cutting caffeine in the afternoon and screens before bed, and a cool, dark, quiet room.
